Medication & Treatment Documentation

Course goals advanced

Spiraling back

This topic revisits grammar you met earlier, in a harder context: Topic 3, Topic 4.

1

Essential Question

Why must numbers, times, names, and details be documented with extreme accuracy?

2

Teaching & Learning Concepts

The communication principles, workplace expectations, and healthcare context behind this topic.

  • Accuracy as a safety property, not a tidiness one
  • Medication safety — the categories of error documentation can prevent
  • Reading labels and orders exactly as written
  • Numbers and units: a misplaced decimal is a tenfold error
  • Timing — when something was given is as important as what
  • Never guessing and never altering information after the fact
3

Grammar Focus

A small set of high-value grammar skills, tied directly to this topic's communication task.

Precision

  • Numbers: write them so they cannot be misread
  • Capitalization of drug names and proper nouns
  • Abbreviations, and the ones that must never be used
  • Punctuation that changes meaning in a dosage
  • Commonly confused words in clinical writing

5

Formative Practice

Guided activities and short exercises. None of this is graded — it is here so you can find out what you know before it counts.

Which entry is correct?

Every option here is something that has appeared in a real record somewhere. Only one is safe.

Practice only — nothing here is graded or recorded.

  • 1Which dosage is written safely?
  • 2Which abbreviation should never be used?
  • 3Which entry documents the time correctly?
  • 4You realize an entry you made an hour ago has the wrong time. What do you do?

6

Cumulative Workplace Product

Combine this topic's grammar, vocabulary, and communication skills into something you would actually produce at work.

Simulated medication / treatment documentation record

Complete a simulated medication or treatment documentation record. Every number, unit, and time must be written so it cannot be misread. Use no abbreviation from the do-not-use list.

Submit through Brightspace. This page is for drafting and self-checking.

7

Revision & Reflection

Review your work against the Communication Check, then name one thing to improve next time.

Communication Check

Check your own writing against all five. Not graded — saved in this browser only.

Communication Check — check each criterion your writing meets

Think about

  • Read every number you wrote as though the decimal point were smudged. Does any of them become a different dose?
  • Could someone reconstruct exactly when each thing happened?
  • Is there any abbreviation here you would not want a tired colleague to interpret at 3am?
